validation.rootTestsNote: Isolated host-root run: DSH_CONTROLS_HOST_ROOT plus the checksum-bound accepted tarball, so no environment-gated host integration case was skipped. A plain node --test without that host seam reports 789 cases with 288 environment-gated skips.
validation.featureEvidence: Two live defects fixed. (1) Execution release treated an Agent instance going away as the execution finishing, but DSH disposes an idle continuable child between runs while its session stays alive and is woken again: an operator screenshot showed eight running subagents against six in the instrument and in the model's own summary. The session's own history proves it: lane i-t192a got a program `released` receipt at 09:30:53 while that child's log records turns at 09:31:14 and 09:44:03 and a wake at 09:51:42, and the same shape holds for i-t176a (released 09:37:40, woke 09:49:32), i-t185a (released 09:38:42, turn 09:42:01, wake 09:51:54) and i-t194a (released ~09:49, turn 09:49:53). The window state machine also forbids `released -> running` in one runtime, so a released lane could never be counted again. Managed executions are now indexed by child session as well as by Agent instance: disposing a continuable child's instance records `unknown` (the admitted slot stays occupied, running is no longer claimed, the binding stays current) and the next wake of the same session re-attaches through the same lease with a `running` receipt, which is a legal transition from unknown. One-shot (`subagent`) instances still release on disposal, and a wake that does not match a known unreleased session still reports unmanaged native activity. (2) The input-area progress dropped the `（参考）` suffix after the T/S ratios: it read as a hedge on the numbers themselves, so the progress line now prints the ratios plainly and keeps the separate note that these windows are accounting observations, not hard quotas.

review.independentReview: none: both changes answer live operator reports with program history as evidence (release receipts versus the child sessions' own turn/wake times). The lifecycle rule is locked by the delegation test, which now asserts that a disposed continuable lane is parked as unknown, that its slot stays admitted, and that the same session waking again returns it to running instead of being reported as unmanaged native activity
